This implies that Ent-Gloeosteretriol may act as a modulator of ICK, influencing its interaction with FbpA. The integration of these pathways indicates that Oblonganoside C could modulate the activity of Ent-Gloeosteretriol, thereby affecting the expression or function of FbpA. The strength of this relationship is supported by the high confidence score of 0.6484, suggesting a plausible biological connection. However, further experimental validation is needed to confirm the direct interaction between Oblonganoside C and FbpA. The mechanism involves a cascade of molecular interactions, where the target of Ent-Gloeosteretriol may play a central role in mediating the effect of Oblonganoside C on FbpA.
